1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from City of Fort St John, about 21 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 56.09888, -120.78685, pull off on an unnamed gravel road. Map links below.
Walk: 1.4 km NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 15 m, about 29 min at 3 km/h.
Hunt: moose, season: VERIFY. Glass the wetland and cutblock edges at dawn and dusk. Move slowly, stop often (Tip). Also: elk, deer (see evidence).
Use: .308 Winchester, 165 to 180 grain premium bullet, shots inside about 200 m (219 yd) (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-32, Region 7B. Season: no general open season (synopsis page 62, 95%). 2 legal flags below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-02, closures 2026-10-16.
R7BC-moose-walk-0004.popWhy: Popular (more hunters): MU 7-32: about 4,897 hunter days a year for moose (2020 to 2024 mean), 1.34 days per square km, top third of BC MUs; access: close to pavement, a town or a rec site. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).
